title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Conclusion
text: Before I knew it, we were back in the village. Just as I was thinking White Day would end without any major issues, I turned to Raphtalia, who had come with me.
“What’s wrong?”
“Could you go check on Gaelion and the Chocolate Monster?”
As I said this, I looked around warily. Yeah, there’s no sign of them right now.
“Naofumi-sama, you’re being too cautious.”
“But—”
“I get it, so just calm down.”

I thought about sleeping somewhere else just for today, but I have to throw a celebration for the folks who worked so hard. The other heroes are supposed to bring their groups over, so I need to get everything ready now.
“Still… is it really okay that the reward is a meal I cooked?”
“That just shows how much everyone loves Naofumi-sama’s cooking.”

It sounds nice, but it’s kind of sad to be stuck doing housework even after saving the world. The mountain of sweets I prepared in advance has dwindled quite a bit—maybe I should restock. After prepping the ingredients for the meal, I’ll have them bring over the returned white chocolate and White Day-themed sweets to replenish the supply. I’ll just sell off the rest to the jewelry merchant through my connections and call it a day.

All that’s left is to make some sweets for the guys who worked so hard. Before I get into the main meal, I’ll make some display sweets. Since it’s White Day, I’ll melt some candy and shape it. Maybe I’ll make it look like ribbons to recreate the musical venue.
Well, to be honest, the only characters I’ll roughly recreate are Filo and Keel. Then, I’ll scatter pudding and marshmallows around the edges and create an arch with the ribbon-shaped candy.
“Seriously, Naofumi-sama’s cooking is just like Magic, isn’t it?”
“It’s not like there’s anything mysterious or anything. Once you get the hang of it, anyone can do this much.”
“Really? I can’t help but think otherwise…”

Next… I guess I’ll whip up some snacks for those two gluttonous Filolials (Filo and the variant)—Filo worked hard, after all. As for the rest, I’ll have the other slaves in charge of cooking handle it. While I was doing all that, the villagers, the heroes, and—incidentally—the Filolials came back.
“Bro, bro! Musicals are so much fun!”
Keel was enthusiastically sharing his thoughts. You’ve been saying that ever since we were at the venue. I guess it really was that much fun, though.
“When’s the next one?”
“That’s up to you. Well, if we don’t perform the same show, people who haven’t seen it won’t get it…”

That said, I’d like to wait a little longer—until the facilities are fully set up—before seriously pursuing a career in acting for Keel. It also depends on whether Zeltoble will even build a facility like an opera house. Part of the reason it sold out was probably because it was a limited-time event. For now, I’ll mix some of Keel’s merchandise into my peddling and see how it goes.
“Come on, you guys, you worked hard today, so eat your fill.”
“Wow… what an amazing ribbon made of candy!”
“Naofumi, you actually made something this elaborate…”
Melty said the same thing to me as Raphtalia did. Hmm… it seems I’m not exactly cut out for confectionery. The heroes said something similar too… Am I the odd one out?

Whether it’s Valentine’s Day or White Day, making your own sweets is what really counts. I’d completely forgotten, but I’d actually delivered flashy chocolate cakes to the weapon shop owner on both Valentine’s Day and White Day as a token of my gratitude for his daily support. A few days later, the old man scolded me for something. He told me not to send him things that left him at a loss for how to react…

Anyway, the villagers finished their meal, and time began to pass slowly. Oh, right… When Motoyasu returned to the village, he was handing out sweets to the Filolials. So that’s the return gift, finally. I guess Filo’s event takes top priority, and the Filolials come second.

Come to think of it, the Filolials are all just like kids. He probably figures he can do it whenever he wants, and there’s no need to rush when dealing with children. Most of the Filolials are just there for an extra round of snacks—only a tiny fraction of them actually looked genuinely happy. Motoyasu really lacks in this area, doesn’t he?
“Cure!”
Jerk!
“I heard Gaelion’s voice! Isn’t he teaming up with the Chocolate Monster to target me again?”
“Naofumi-sama, please calm down. We’re keeping them under strict supervision, aren’t we?”

Just to be safe, I’ve ordered Taniko to separate Gaelion and the Chocolate Monster and keep an eye on them. The Chocolate Monster claims it’s learned its lesson and won’t go on a rampage, but who knows how things will turn out.
“Cureeeeeee!”
“Isn’t that a death cry!?”
“Take a closer look.”

Looking in the direction Raphtalia was pointing, I saw a mutant Filolial playfully licking the tip of Gaelion’s tail. Gaelion seemed to be resisting, looking annoyed, but since the other one had no ill intent, he couldn’t bring himself to bare his fangs—he looked rather flustered. Well, he’s leveled up quite a bit by now, so I don’t think he’ll be able to shoo it away unless he really goes all out. Come to think of it, for someone who usually looks so sleepy, he’s being surprisingly playful. Since Gaelion’s so big, it feels like he’s just being toyed with in his baby dragon mode.
“Hey, what are they doing?”
“Hm?”
Filo is watching the scene while munching on the snacks I made.
“Well, there’s this little girl and one of Filo’s subordinates—they’re licking Gaelion while telling him they like him.”
“……Like him?”
“Filo, please stop calling the Raph-species ‘little me.’”
“Okay. That girl really likes Gaelion, you know?”
“Why?”
Don’t Filolials hate dragons? Well, technically speaking, he’s not a true Filolial. Oh, Gaelion started growling menacingly. She’s responding with a “kue kue” sound.
“Looks like she just confessed to him? Um… she said it’s because the chocolate was so delicious.”

As a result of the extraordinary practice Gaelion put in for the sake of his love for me, he’s become the best chocolate maker in the village. Well, making other sweets from chocolate is a whole different process, so I guess I’m still better at that.
“That’s why she likes him—she’s saying she wants him to make it for her for the rest of her life.”
“For a Filolial half-breed, she’s got a pretty weird personality, doesn’t she?”

Actually, she tried to eat her own kind without batting an eye, so she might be a different species altogether. Maybe her gluttony comes from the Filolial side, while the rest of her is more like a Raph-species? Raphtalia can be violent sometimes… though she doesn’t get angry without a reason. I’m the same way, actually. It’s just individual differences—it has nothing to do with her parents. But I’d say her Filolial instincts are pretty weak.
“Why are you looking at me?”
“I just thought, ‘Her Raph-species blood must be too strong to be linked to that personality.’”
“Huh…”
“Isn’t it Naofumi’s fault?”

Melty muttered as she watched the scene unfold. She’d been watching the race involving Filo and the others with great excitement. Melty is the type to get into arguments with Taniko about Filolial ecology.
“What are you talking about? I’m not a glutton.”
“If you grew up eating nothing but Naofumi’s cooking, you’d become a gourmet too. Just look at Filo.”
Raphtalia looked at Filo, me, and the mutant, then nodded as if she’d come to some realization.
“I see.”
“Why are you nodding in agreement right there?”
“I can understand why he’d prioritize his appetite over his instincts. Either way, confessing to a dragon is pretty weird… Well, Gaelion is totally devoted to Naofumi, though.”
“Cut it out. You’re going to make my trauma flare up again.”
“Okay, okay. Naofumi, why don’t you be supportive—or better yet, encourage him?”

Come to think of it, she’s right. If that mutant can keep Gaelion tied up, that’d be a huge win. In fact, whether it’s a fait accompli or whatever, I should make Gaelion doubt himself—create an excuse to reject him later, saying, ‘I absolutely won’t date someone who isn’t devoted to me!’
“Go for it! Seduce that gay dragon!”
“Naofumi-sama, please support me in your heart.”

“C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C Hah… Who’s going to save him, you fool!”
“Well, it’ll probably be good therapy for his body… but a hybrid of a Filolial and a new species of monster—that’s quite a strange combination.”
Even Gaelion’s parent seems to have given up on him somewhat.
“Kueh!”

The mutant is clamping down on Gaelion’s tail right at the base and sucking on it. Is this some kind of kink? Gaelion looks like he’s desperately trying to hold back. Even Taniko—who, as expected, knows about Gaelion’s perverted tastes—isn’t saying anything. She looks like she’s just hoping this rough treatment will make him stop targeting me.

Hm? I spot a rare guy watching the scene with flames of jealousy rising in his eyes. The Thoroughbred is staring at Gaelion and the mutant from the shadows of the building. But his gaze is seriously scary. Since this one is a Filolial, Gaelion should be genetically repulsed by it. So… wait? Does that guy actually like the mutant?

I’d forgotten, but the Thoroughbred is male and the mutant is female. So when he’d been eyeing her as a Rival, was he actually just interested and trying to tease her? He’s just as much of a pain in the neck as his foster parent. He’s so fast, he must be a total heartthrob… so why on earth is he falling for that high-maintenance one? And on top of that, even after nearly getting eaten by her, he still likes her?

Come to think of it, for Filolials, showing that you’re superior to your partner is part of their courtship behavior. In other words, since this guy takes pride in his speed, he had to outrun the Variant.

Yeah. Children take after their parents. It’s all well and good to analyze it that way, but by that logic, that guy and I would end up being similar. Let me just say right now: I’m not like that. In my case, I’ll just chalk it up to how I was raised.
“CUREEEEEEEEEEE!”
Gaelion’s scream echoed through the village. Just as… White Day was drawing to a close.
“Hey.”
Taniko beckoned me over.
“Big bro!”
And Keel, too, for good measure.
“What’s up?”
“Well, you see. The Chocolate Monster that Wyndia-chan was taking care of—”
“I told you to get rid of it if it caused any trouble, didn’t I?”
“No… it says it wants to talk to you.”

Talk? I don’t have anything to talk about. I don’t even have anything to talk about in the first place. But if I just leave it alone, who knows what trouble it might cause. Taniko pointed at the Chocolate Monster standing in front of the crepe tree and replied. I had all the heroes prepare for battle and stand by, ready to engage at any moment.
“What is it?”
I asked after we’d formed a perimeter. Then, a faint light began to rise from the Chocolate Monster.
“It’s about… time, apparently.”
“Time for what?”
“The Chocolate Monster is only around for a limited time, right? It’s saying that time is almost up.”
“So?”
I hold my shield out in front of me, fully prepared to run if anything happens, and stay on high alert. Taniko continues, her attitude making it obvious at a glance that she thinks I’m overreacting.
“It’s saying ‘goodbye’ because it’s about to disappear.”

The white Chocolate Monster is waving goodbye to me, the villagers, and Gaelion. I see. Go ahead and disappear already. With this, I can finally say goodbye to those days of living in fear of chocolate.

“I was able to spend a very meaningful and happy Valentine’s Day and White Day this year. Sure, I went a little too wild… but I’m grateful that, in all my time as a Chocolate Monster, I’ve never had such an active time as this.”

He’s trying to wrap this up as a heartwarming story, but I won’t forget. Because I ate Gaelion’s chocolate, I went on a rampage and tried to fulfill Gaelion’s wish! It’s all your fault I’ve been traumatized! One wrong move and I would’ve been impregnated!

The Chocolate Monster floated gently, glowing with a soft light as it became translucent and faded away. It kept staring at us as it headed toward the crepe tree, waving goodbye before flying off and disappearing.
“It said it’ll come back next year.”
“Don’t ever come back.”
“Naofumi-sama… I understand how you feel, but it’s such a beautiful sight…”

The light emitted by the Chocolate Monster rained down like snow all around us before fading away. The other heroes seemed captivated by the fantastical scene, but I couldn’t bring myself to enjoy it. The faint light formed a ribbon that tied together the hands of Itsuki and Rishia, who were happily holding hands, creating a scene reminiscent of a red thread before vanishing.
In Ren’s case, it was Taniko and the female knight. As for Motoyasu… the Filolials… the ribbon seemed to be floating above them cheerfully. He tried to reach out to Filo, but she dodged him.

And then… the light I’d scattered over the villagers gathered above me, took on some sort of shape, and fell right in front of my eyes. The light lingered there as if urging me to catch it… so I knocked it away.
“Naofumi-sama, please, just read the room and take it.”
“N-o-w-a-y! Who says I’m clueless?”
“Sigh… I knew it.”

Raphtalia picked it up and took my hand. Then—perhaps it was the villagers’ inner voices—even though no one was speaking, I could sense voices saying “thank you” and feelings of “I love you” coming through. Being thanked like that all over again makes me feel a little awkward. But I didn’t want to accept it through a phenomenon like this.
“But… why did it disappear toward the crepe tree?”
“I don’t know…”
I have a very bad feeling about this.

Some time later… I’ll note here that Keel came to report—as a truly trivial matter—that the crepe tree had become more powerful. Specifically, the taste of the chocolate sauce had improved, and the overall quality had gotten better. Also, the trunk had thickened, and it seems to be growing little by little. I’d hate for it to eventually grow as big as the World Tree, but I remember Keel saying his ambition was to make it a huge tree visible even from afar.

Another completely trivial note… the following year, the same chocolate monster—or so it seemed—appeared in my territory and spent some time in the village. To dispose of a monster that’s invulnerable even when blown to smithereens, you have to bend the laws of nature using the power of spirits—but the spirits wouldn’t… lend their power for something so trivial.
In a way, that creature is just like a spirit. What on earth is a chocolate spirit, anyway…?
Well, that’s more or less how Valentine’s Day and White Day passed by.
